message.reasoning:
We need to analyze method behavior and identify all possible exception scenarios for max(Indicator<Num>) method. The existing test cases already cover many scenarios, including null argument leading to NullPointerException, NaN handling, infinities, same instance, commutativity, derived indicator. But we need to find any other exception scenarios not covered.

Potential exceptions: 
- Passing an Indicator that throws exception when getValue is called (e.g., indicator with out-of-bounds index). But max returns a NumericIndicator that will call getValue on both delegates when its getValue is invoked. So exception could be IndexOutOfBoundsException when index out of range. However test case should trigger exception at creation? The method itself just creates BinaryOperation.max(this, other) which likely checks null only. So only immediate exception is NullPointerException for null argument. However there could be IllegalArgumentException if other delegate is of different BarSeries? Possibly BinaryOperation.max may check that both indicators belong to same series. If they have different BarSeries, maybe throws IllegalArgumentException. Not covered.

Also possible exception if other is a NumericIndicator that wraps null delegate? But NumericIndicator.of probably throws IllegalArgumentException if delegate null. Not sure.

Thus we can add test cases for mismatched BarSeries leading to IllegalArgumentException (or IllegalStateException). Need to guess actual exception thrown by BinaryOperation.max. Look at TA4J library: BinaryOperation.max likely checks both indicators are not null and have same BarSeries. In TA4J, many binary operations check series equality and throw IllegalArgumentException if not same. So we can add test case.

Also test for other being a NumericIndicator with null underlying delegate (unlikely). But we can test passing an indicator that returns null Num (maybe NullPointerException when comparing). However Num implementation likely never null.

Thus we add new group: "NumericIndicator.max(Indicator<Num>) - different BarSeries". Cases: create two BarSeries with different lengths; create ConstantIndicator on each; call max; expect IllegalArgumentException.

Also test for other being a non-Indicator (compile-time not possible). So only that.

Also test for other being a NumericIndicator that is itself a BinaryOperation that fails due to internal null? Not.

Thus we output JSON with new group(s). Must avoid duplication with existing. Provide only new test cases.

Return array of groups with cases.

Let's craft JSON.

Group name: "NumericIndicator.max(Indicator<Num>) - different BarSeries". Cases: one.

Input: other: "ConstantIndicator of Num values [10,20,30] built on a different BarSeries". Expected: "IllegalArgumentException". Description: "When the other indicator belongs to a different BarSeries than this indicator, max should throw IllegalArgumentException because operations require same series."

Potential also test for other being a NumericIndicator with mismatched series (same as above). Provide.

Also maybe test for other being a NumericIndicator that is null after of? Not.

Thus output JSON array with this group.
